# Pattern Review: Brackenford Hall

## Input Quality and Limitations

The fictional log covers two distinct events in one month, with one occurrence per event. Both diagnoses have supporting evidence: technicians reproduced the failures, measured damaged cables, replaced them, and observed the faults stop. No material ambiguity affects the counts. The log does not establish why the cables became damaged.

## Summary

| Candidate | Occurrences | Distinct Instances | Cause Consistency | Confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Visual content disappearing | 2 | 2 | Both traced to damaged cables | High for the shared symptom topic |
| Damaged cables causing display failures | 2 | 2 | Independently reproduced, measured and resolved by replacement | High within this log; limited to two events |

## Genuine Patterns

E1 (“The screen goes black”) and E2 (“Slides keep vanishing”) use different wording but share the same evidenced cause: a damaged cable. Each diagnosis was independently supported by reproduction, measurement and successful replacement.

This is a genuine repeated driver across two distinct instances. No contradictory diagnosis is recorded. Confidence is high for recurrence within this log, but the sample does not establish a wider or persistent problem.

## Misleading Surface Patterns

None demonstrated. The differing descriptions should not be split into separate causes: both were traced to damaged cables. Equally, neither description alone would have established that diagnosis.

## Isolated Signals, Not Yet Patterns

None at the recorded cause level. Each event is distinct, and the damaged-cable finding has support from both.

## Suggested Actions for Human Approval

A person should check both diagnoses and decide whether the recurrence merits further investigation. If warranted, investigate how the cables were damaged before selecting a preventive fix or process change. Neither is already decided.

## What This Sample Cannot Tell You

The log cannot establish a failure rate, a longer-term trend, a shared reason for cable damage, or whether other rooms or future events are affected. It supports two cable-related failures, not a conclusion about venue-wide equipment quality or handling practices.
